content: The test image shows a whole plant with leaves displaying mosaic/mottled yellow-green and green patterns with leaf distortion - pointing strongly to a viral disease. Top candidates from the leaf part index: Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Verticillium_Wilt.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image features:** Diffuse yellow-green mosaic/mottling pattern across leaves, mild leaf puckering/distortion, plant appears lighter in overall color, bushy appearance.

**Reference image comparisons:**
1. CMV leaf (Bugwood_1/4): Shows shoestring distortion - partial match (distortion present but less extreme in test image)
2. TSWV leaf (Bugwood_11): Ring spots/concentric circles - no match
3. Verticillium Wilt (LeafNet_265): V-shaped brown necrosis - no match
4. Leaf Mold (CDDM_313): Bleached spots - no match
5. Powdery Mildew (CDDM_116): White powdery patches - no match
6. Bacterial Speck (Bugwood_14): Small black specks - no match
7. CMV whole_plant (Bugwood_18): Field shot - consistent with lighter-colored, mottled plants
8. CMV second leaf view confirmed mosaic pattern

The yellow-green mosaic, interveinal chlorosis, leaf distortion, and overall lighter plant coloration most closely match Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus, even though the reference shoestring symptoms are more severe than shown. No other class produces this diffuse mottled/mosaic chlorosis pattern.
